6 fence/pane/wall block(s) have no north/east/south/west set although a neighbour would connect, so they show as lone posts: (6, 0, 2), (6, 0, 4), (1, 2, 3) and 3 more.
No door on the front half (z = 0 is the front, toward the easel).
The roof does not reach past the walls on any two opposite sides: give it one block of overhang.

visual.summary: Level 3 adds barrels and a lantern but is the same all-oak box; the props are scattered, not a work yard.
problems: Everything is the same oak colour: use the style A palette, with a cobblestone plinth, spruce or dark oak posts and beams, white terracotta or oak plank infill and a darker spruce roof
The roof sits flush with the side walls: give it one block of overhang all round, with upside-down stairs under the gable ends
Make it read as a carpenter's yard: a log pile, a sawhorse (fence plus slab), planks stacked on a slab, a chopping block and a lantern by the open bay
The door is at the back; the front (toward the easel) should hold the door or the open work bay
Add life: a flower box under the window, a few leaves or vines at a corner

visual.summary: Close: a clear little workshop with props and good colours; flat side walls and a one-colour roof keep it just under the bar.
problems: Make it read as a carpenter from level 1: the log pile and the sawhorse should be there from the start, not only at level 2
Give the side windows trapdoor shutters and a slab sill at level 1, so the plaster walls aren't flat panels
The roof is one spruce brown: mix in a row of dark oak stairs at the eaves or along the gable edge
